name: Gradium Phonon TTS family (phonon-31m-en, phonon-40m-en/fr/de/es/pt/multilingual)

lineage.base_model: builds on Kyutai Pocket TTS and the Mimi codec (card)
lineage.family: Phonon (Gradium; not Fermion Research's Phonon ASR)

purpose: 'High-quality Text-to-Speech, on your device': natural 24 kHz streaming speech small enough for a browser tab, a phone or a laptop CPU (card).

license.name: phonon-31m-en: Apache-2.0; all phonon-40m-* models: CC-BY-NC-4.0
license.notes: phonon-31m-en repo has an Apache-2.0 LICENSE file (header opened) and the card table lists Apache 2.0 for it. The 40m English/French/German/Spanish/Portuguese/multilingual models are CC BY-NC 4.0 per the card table and HF tags: non-commercial only. phonon-40m-de is gated on HF (auto-approve), so its own card was not readable; licence taken from the family table and tags. Texts not read in full. Verdict policy (README, 2026-11-19): this licence term does not lower tona_fit; kept here for an installer label.

architecture.kind: flow-matching transformer predicting Mimi audio latents one 80 ms frame at a time (31M parameters, d_model 512, 6 layers) + Mimi decoder; streaming, 24 kHz mono
architecture.why_this_design: Builder says it builds on Pocket TTS and the Mimi codec of Kyutai for tiny, streaming on-device synthesis (card).

weaknesses: German and the other non-English voices are CC BY-NC: not usable commercially
no cloning mentioned for the open models in the part of the card I read
soft.maturity: phonon-31m-en 343k downloads in a month, 172 likes; Gradium (voice-AI company).

tona_fit.reason: Excellent size, and phonon-40m-de is a German voice in 75 MB; phonon-31m-en is the English option. Compare quality against Kokoro/Kitten/Pocket-class models before any offer.
